<a id="directorypacksource"></a>

## `DirectoryPackSource`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Packs.DirectoryPackSource` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Implements: [`IPackSource`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#ipacksource)

An [`IPackSource`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#ipacksource) backed by one folder under `CWYLS Mods/`. Reading is done once, in the constructor, so a pack that changes on disk mid-scan cannot produce a manifest and a file listing that disagree.

Nothing here throws: a pack folder is untrusted input, and an unreadable one must be reported as a skipped pack, not as an exception that stops every other pack from loading. Every failure is logged and turned into a missing manifest or an empty listing.

<a id="directorypacksource--files"></a>

### `IReadOnlyList<string> Files { get; }`

Every file in the pack, relative to the pack root, in any separator style; [`PackContentIndex.Build`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packcontentindex--build) normalises them. Never null.

<a id="directorypacksource--foldername"></a>

### `string FolderName { get; }`

The pack's folder name, for a message that has to point at a directory.

<a id="directorypacksource--id"></a>

### `string Id { get; }`

How this candidate is named in reports *before* its manifest has been read - normally the folder name. Once the manifest parses, its own `id` takes over.

<a id="directorypacksource--manifesttext"></a>

### `string ManifestText { get; }`

The whole text of the pack's `manifest.json`, or null when the folder has none or it could not be read. Null is [`PackSkipReason.MissingManifest`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packskipreason--missingmanifest).

<a id="directorypacksource--rootpath"></a>

### `string RootPath { get; }`

Absolute path of the pack folder.

<a id="directorypacksource--read"></a>

### `static DirectoryPackSource Read(string rootPath)`

Reads one pack folder.

**Parameters**

- `rootPath`: Absolute path of the folder, e.g. `<CWYLS Mods>/cwy.example`.

**Returns:** A source describing the folder. A folder with no readable `manifest.json` still produces a source, with a null [`DirectoryPackSource.ManifestText`](#directorypacksource--manifesttext), so the resolver can report it as [`PackSkipReason.MissingManifest`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packskipreason--missingmanifest) rather than silently ignoring it.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentException`: `rootPath` is null or blank.

## `LoadedPack`

sealed class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Packs.LoadedPack` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

A pack that passed every gate and is installed on this machine: the Core-side [`ResolvedPack`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#resolvedpack) plus the absolute folder its files live in.

This is the type the features consume - they open [`LoadedPack.Index`](#loadedpack--index) entries through [`LoadedPack.FullPath`](#loadedpack--fullpath-packfile) to read textures, audio and data files - so it is deliberately the only place where a pack's contents and its location meet.

**Parameters**

- `rootPath`: Absolute path of the pack folder.
- `index`: The classified contents of that folder.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException`: `manifest` or `index` is null.
- `ArgumentException`: `rootPath` is null or blank.

<a id="packmanager"></a>

## `PackManager`

static class · `CwyLs.ModLoader.Packs.PackManager` · assembly `CwyLs.ModLoader`

Discovers the content packs installed in [`ModLoaderPaths.PacksRoot`](CwyLs.ModLoader.md#modloaderpaths--packsroot), resolves them with [`PackResolver`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packresolver), and holds the result for the rest of the framework.

Static because packs are process-wide: CwyLs.ModLoader.Bulbul, the smoke plugin and any third party mod all need the same list, and they are separate BepInEx assemblies with no reference to one another.

**Adding a pack needs a game restart.** Packs are read once, during [`ModLoaderPlugin`](CwyLs.ModLoader.md#modloaderplugin)'s Awake, before the game has loaded anything they might patch. [`PackManager.Rescan`](#packmanager--rescan) exists for the smoke checks and for development; it refreshes this list but does *not* undo or re-apply anything a previous scan's packs already did.

Every scan ends by raising [`PackManager.PacksResolved`](#packmanager--packsresolved) with its [`PackResolution`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packresolution) and then [`PackManager.PacksChanged`](#packmanager--packschanged), the argument-free form kept for existing subscribers.

Config key of the game-version override (ignores `minGameVersion`/`maxGameVersion`).

Config section holding the pack settings.

<a id="packmanager--coreversion"></a>

### `static SemVer CoreVersion { get; }`

This framework's API version (`CwyApi.Version`), as compared against a pack's or code mod's `loaderVersion`.

<a id="packmanager--enabled"></a>

### `static bool Enabled { get; }`

True when pack loading is switched on (`Packs.Enabled`, default true).

<a id="packmanager--hasscanned"></a>

### `static bool HasScanned { get; }`

True once a scan has completed, successfully or not.

<a id="packmanager--ignoregameversion"></a>

### `static bool IgnoreGameVersion { get; }`

True when a pack is loaded even though the running game is outside its `minGameVersion`/`maxGameVersion` range (`Packs.IgnoreGameVersion`, default false); it then logs a warning instead of being skipped. A different `gameVersion` alone never skips a pack, with or without this switch.

<a id="packmanager--lastresolution"></a>

### `static PackResolution LastResolution { get; }`

The resolution of the last completed scan - the same object the last [`PackManager.PacksResolved`](#packmanager--packsresolved) carried. Never null; [`PackResolution.Empty`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packresolution--empty) before the first scan and while pack loading is switched off.

<a id="packmanager--lastscanerror"></a>

### `static string LastScanError { get; }`

The failure of the last scan, or null when it completed. A scan only fails as a whole for something outside any one pack - an unreadable `CWYLS Mods` folder, say; a single bad pack is a [`SkippedPack`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#skippedpack), not a scan failure.

<a id="packmanager--loaded"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<LoadedPack> Loaded { get; }`

The packs that loaded, in dependency order: a pack always appears after the packs it depends on. Never null; empty before the first scan.

<a id="packmanager--skipped"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<SkippedPack> Skipped { get; }`

Packs that were found but refused, with reasons. Never null.

<a id="packmanager--warnings"></a>

### `static IReadOnlyList<PackWarning> Warnings { get; }`

Packs that loaded with a warning in the last scan (e.g. made for another game version), one entry per pack. Never null.

<a id="packmanager--packschanged"></a>

### `static event Action PacksChanged`

The argument-free form of [`PackManager.PacksResolved`](#packmanager--packsresolved), raised immediately after it for subscribers that only need to know that something moved. Prefer [`PackManager.PacksResolved`](#packmanager--packsresolved) in new code: it hands you the same resolution the framework logged, instead of making you re-read [`PackManager.Loaded`](#packmanager--loaded) and hope nothing scanned in between.

<a id="packmanager--packsresolved"></a>

### `static event Action<PackResolution> PacksResolved`

Raised after every completed scan, including the first, with the resolution that scan produced - what loaded, in what order, what was refused and why, and the one-line [`PackResolution.Summary`](CwyLs.ModLoader.Core.Packs.md#packresolution--summary). Handlers run on the thread that scanned (the Unity main thread in practice) and a handler that throws is logged and skipped, never allowed to abort the scan or the handlers after it.

A scan that failed as a whole re-raises the previous resolution rather than an empty one, matching [`PackManager.Loaded`](#packmanager--loaded): a failed rescan loses nothing that already loaded.

<a id="packmanager--discoverandload"></a>

### `static void DiscoverAndLoad(ConfigFile config = null)`

Binds the config, registers the P1 smoke checks and performs the first scan. Called once from [`ModLoaderPlugin`](CwyLs.ModLoader.md#modloaderplugin)'s Awake; calling it again simply rescans.

**Parameters**

- `config`: Config file the `Packs.*` entries are bound in. Pass the calling plugin's `Config`; when omitted the framework binds them in its own .cfg.

<a id="packmanager--find"></a>

### `static LoadedPack Find(string id)`

The loaded pack with this id, or null when it is not loaded.

**Parameters**

- `id`: A pack id, e.g. `cwy.example`.

<a id="packmanager--findskipped"></a>

### `static SkippedPack FindSkipped(string id)`

The skip record for this id or folder name, or null when it was not skipped.

**Parameters**

- `id`: A pack id, or the folder name of a pack whose manifest never parsed.

<a id="packmanager--rescan"></a>

### `static bool Rescan()`

Repeats the scan and refreshes [`PackManager.Loaded`](#packmanager--loaded) and [`PackManager.Skipped`](#packmanager--skipped). For the smoke checks and for development only - see the note on the class about restarting.

**Returns:** True when the scan completed; false when it failed (see [`PackManager.LastScanError`](#packmanager--lastscanerror)).

<a id="packmanager--rescan-bool"></a>

### `static bool Rescan(bool quiet)`

Repeats the scan, optionally without warning about the packs it skips.

**Parameters**

- `quiet`: True to report skipped packs at Info instead of Warning. For a caller that planted the broken pack on purpose: `p1.packs.bad_manifest_skipped` writes a truncated manifest to prove the resolver refuses it, and the resulting `WARN pack skipped: _smoke_bad (InvalidManifest)` was the check working, read as the framework failing. A real startup scan stays loud.

**Returns:** True when the scan completed; false when it failed (see [`PackManager.LastScanError`](#packmanager--lastscanerror)).
